Hi there! I’m your Business Analyst for the BioVault Lab Specimen Tracker project.

I see you want a desktop system to track cryogenic bio‑specimens, handle accessioning, generate 2D barcodes, and manage freezer chain‑of‑custody. I’ll ask a few focused questions to turn that idea into clear, testable requirements the team can build.

Mind if I ask a few questions to get started?
Yes, please proceed with the discovery questions.

Got it – you’re looking to build a desktop app for tracking cryogenic specimens, handling accessioning, barcode generation, and freezer chain‑of‑custody.

1. What specific problem or pain point are you trying to solve with this system? (Understanding the core need helps shape every requirement.)  
2. Can you describe the main user types (e.g., lab tech, PI, compliance officer) and what each needs to do in the app? (We’ll map features to personas.)  
3. Roughly how many specimens will be managed and how many users will be using the system at the same time? (Numbers let us size performance and storage.)

The primary problem is misplacing cryogenic biological samples stored across -80C freezers and liquid nitrogen tanks. Technicians spend 25 minutes per retrieval with manual paper logs, causing cold-chain compliance risks.

Got it—misplaced samples and long manual retrievals are hurting compliance and efficiency.

1. Which user roles will use the system and what core tasks should each be able to do? (We need to map features to personas.)  
2. Approximately how many specimens will be tracked in total and what peak number of concurrent users do you expect? (Numbers guide storage and performance.)  
3. How will you know the new system is successful—e.g., reduced retrieval time, fewer misplaced samples, compliance audit scores, or something else? (Defines success metrics.)

Primary users are: 1. Lab Technician (P-01) scanning 2D DataMatrix barcodes and logging freezer rack/shelf/box positions; 2. Principal Investigator (P-02) searching sample inventory and requesting pulls; 3. Compliance Officer (P-03) auditing chain-of-custody logs.

Thanks for clarifying the three user types and their core duties.

1. How many specimens do you expect to track initially, and what growth rate (e.g., +10 % per year) do you anticipate? Knowing volume helps size the database and performance targets.  
2. Which measurable outcomes will tell you the system is successful (e.g., cut retrieval time to ≤ 10 min, < 1 % misplaced samples, audit compliance score ≥ 95 %)? These define our success metrics.  
3. Do you need the tracker to talk to any existing tools—such as a LIMS, barcode printer, or freezer inventory spreadsheet? If so, what data should flow each way? This shapes integration scope.

Key workflow: Technician receives specimen vial, scans barcode, assigns box coordinate (e.g. Freezer 2, Rack B, Shelf 3, Box 12, Position E4), verifies temperature threshold, and saves record. Any temperature alert flag requires supervisor sign-off.

Got it – the tech will scan a vial’s 2‑D barcode, log its exact freezer location, check the temperature, and flag any alerts for a supervisor’s sign‑off.

1. How many specimens do you expect to have in the system at launch, and what annual growth rate (e.g., +10 % / year) do you anticipate? Numbers let us size the database and performance targets.  
2. Which concrete metrics will tell you the system is successful? For example, target retrieval time (≤ 10 min), misplaced‑sample rate (< 1 %), audit compliance score (≥ 95 %). These become your success criteria.  
3. Will the tracker need to talk to any existing tools – such as a LIMS, barcode printer, or temperature‑monitoring system? If so, what data should flow each way (e.g., send specimen IDs to LIMS, receive temperature alerts, print labels)? This defines the integration scope.

All data must be stored locally in SQLite with zero cloud database dependency. System must run offline on laboratory desktop workstations (macOS and Windows 11). UI response time must be under 1.5 seconds for barcode scans.

Got it – you need everything stored locally in SQLite, the app must work offline on macOS and Windows 11 desktops, and barcode scans need to respond within 1.5 seconds.

1. Can you walk me through a typical end‑to‑end workflow for each user type (Technician, PI, Compliance Officer)? What steps does each role take from start to finish when using the system? (We need clear user journeys.)  
2. Which features are must‑haves for the MVP versus nice‑to‑have for later releases? (That defines the project scope.)  
3. The budget is $15 k and you have a 6‑week target for v1. Are there any hard constraints on staffing or milestones we should bake into the timeline? (Helps lock down timeline & budget.)
